bill_title: Cloture Motion to End Filibuster: Craig Becker NLRB Confirmation
aflcio_description: President Obama nominated the highly qualified and respected labor lawyer Craig Becker to the National Labor Relations Board. Republican senators, with the backing of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and other Big Business interests, filibustered his nomination. A cloture motion to end the filibuster failed Feb. 9 by a vote of 52–33 (60 votes were needed). In March, Obama used a recess appointment to put Becker on the NLRB.

bill_title: Hiring Incentives to Restore Employment Act
aflcio_description: The bill provides employers with incentives to hire and retain new employees, including extending enhanced small business expensing and providing state and local governments with the ability to issue special purpose tax credit bonds for school construction, energy conservation and renewable energy. It extends the Surface Transportation Act until Dec. 31, 2010. The Senate voted to invoke cloture to limit debate.

John Thune (R-S.D.) to the Unemployment Compensation Extension Act of 2010 (H.R. 4213) would have repealed Davis-Bacon coverage for projects funded under this bill. The Davis-Bacon Act requires companies to pay construction workers locally prevailing wages on federally funded projects. The amendment failed.

bill_title: FAA Air Transportation Modernization and Safety Improvement Act
aflcio_description: This bill provides $34 billion of funding over two years, which will create 150,000 jobs per year, according to the DPC. The bill modernizes the air traffic control system and improves the safety, reliability and availability of U.S. air transportation.

aflcio_description: The Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act of 2010 makes substantial improvements to the Senate-passed health reform bill, H.R. 3590. It closes the Medicare prescription drug "donut hole" and improves the affordability provisions for low- and moderate-income families. It increases federal support to help states expand their Medicaid programs to cover the most needy and makes fairer the penalty on employers who fail to offer coverage to their workers. It also eliminates 85 percent of the excise tax on premiums and instead makes the Medicare payroll tax fairer to working families by applying it to unearned income. The Senate took up the bill under reconciliation rules, which make the bill filibuster-proof and require only a simple majority to pass the bill.

bill_title: Amendment to Reduce the Concentration of Financial Institution Power
aflcio_description: Sen. Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio) offered an amendment to the Restoring American Financial Stability Act of 2010 to address the domination of the financial system by institutions that are deemed "too big to fail." The Brown amendment would reduce the concentration of financial power and the risk many of these institutions pose to the economy and restore an even playing field for community banks by imposing leverage and liability limits on bank holding companies and financial companies. It would have imposed a strict cap (ten percent of insured depository institutions total U.S. deposits) on the amount of deposits held by any bank or thrift and would have limited the non-deposit liabilities of a bank. The amendment needed 60 votes to pass.

bill_title: Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act
aflcio_description: The Restoring American Financial Stability Act of 2010 reins in Wall Street's and Big Bank's dangerous practices and products that crashed the economy. Among other provisions, the bill improves accountability and transparency in the financial system, brings to an end "too big to fail" institutions, protects American taxpayers by ending bailouts and protects consumers from abusive financial services practices.

aflcio_description: The Senate and House both passed legislation to rein in Wall Street's and Big Banks' dangerous practices and products that crashed the economy. The conference report that melded the two bills creates a new federal agency to oversee consumer financial products, brings the derivatives market under significant federal regulation for the first time and gives company shareholders and regulators greater say on executive pay packages.

bill_title: Cloture Motion: Unemployment Compensation Extension Act of 2010
aflcio_description: During the first part of 2010, Senate Republicans mounted several filibusters against extending the federal unemployment insurance (UI) program for long-term jobless workers. A motion to invoke cloture and end the filibuster against the bill that extended the UI program to Nov 30 and made it retroactive to June 2 was approved.

bill_title: Confirmation of Elena Kagan to the U.S. Supreme Court
aflcio_description: Confirmation of President Obama's nomination of Elena Kagan of Massachusetts to be an associate justice of the U.S. Supreme Court.

bill_title: Resolution Overturning Modernized Union Election Rules for Airline and Rail Workers
corrections: vote_question cloture -> motion: senate.gov gives roll 636 of the 111th a `majority_requirement` of 1/2, so no cloture was involved - S.J.Res. 30 is a Congressional Review Act disapproval resolution, whose motion to proceed is privileged and non-debatable. It drew no other roll call in the Congress, so there was no vote on passage, and a motion to proceed does not dispose of the measure. The record's own text says so: 'The motion to proceed to consider the measure was rejected in the Senate'
aflcio_description: The National Mediation Board issued a new rule in May 2010 that calls for the majority of votes cast to determine the outcome of union representation elections for airline and rail workers—in the same way elections are decided in congressional and other democratic elections. Previously, a worker who did not cast a vote was instead counted as "No" vote. This resolution of disapproval would roll back the NMB's democratic, union representation election rule. The motion to proceed to consider the measure was rejected in the Senate.

bill_title: Creating American Jobs and Ending Offshoring Act
corrections: vote_question 'passage' -> 'cloture': the roll call's own question is 'On the Cloture Motion'. The scorecard's value was inferred from its prose, which the 11 Aug 2026 review measured at ~8% wrong
aflcio_description: To encourage U.S. firms to keep jobs in America and discourage companies for exporting U.S. jobs, the bill would provide U.S. companies a two-year reduction in their share of Social Security payroll taxes for new employees hired to replace workers performing similar duties overseas. It would be paid for by repealing various tax breaks for companies that close plants in the U.S. and move operations overseas. The motion failed by a 53-45 vote (60 votes were needed to pass).

bill_title: Public Safety Employer-Employee Cooperation Act of 2010
aflcio_description: The legislation would extend bargaining rights to police and firefighters in states that do not allow such public safety workers to join unions. More than 20 states do not fully protect those bargaining rights and Virginia and North Carolina prohibit public safety employees from collective bargaining. A motion to end a Republican filibuster against public safety workers' rights bill failed by a 55-43 vote (60 votes were needed to pass).
